name: Crystal Ball
notes: Placements and run periods at SPEAR and DORIS II are derived from "three years" and "five years" statements (see the interval notes); AIP says the SPEAR experiment "completed running in 1979", which contradicts this and is recorded as a conflict in the log.
The detector later ran at the Brookhaven AGS and at the Mainz MAMI accelerator; those hadron-physics programmes are not part of this record.

physics_goals.locator: AIP Study of Multi-Institutional Collaborations, SLAC-SP-024
physics_goals.quote: Although proposed before discovery of the J/psi, the detector was well suited to and primarily used for studying the spectra of charm-quark systems.
physics_goals.value: Study the spectra of charm-quark systems (charmonium) at SPEAR

summary.plain: A spherical detector of 672 sodium iodide crystals that surrounded the collision point to measure photons. Built at SLAC and used at SPEAR for charmonium spectroscopy, then moved to DESY's DORIS ring in 1982 to study bottom-quark systems, before going to Brookhaven and Mainz for later work.
summary.technical: Crystal Ball: 672 NaI(Tl) crystals covering 94% of 4π, central spark chambers; approved 1975 (SLAC-SP-024, spokesperson E. D. Bloom); about three years of meson spectroscopy at SPEAR, then about five years at DORIS II (DESY) studying b-quark systems; in storage at SLAC 1987-1996, then at BNL (hadron physics, not recorded here).
